ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Within-subjects impossible for learning manipulation; df in ANOVA tables inconsistent
ground_truth.original_snippet: We embedded Studies 1 and 3 of Small et al. (2007) into a single between-subject design with identifiability and intervention as the independent variables;
ground_truth.modified_snippet: We embedded Studies 1 and 3 of Small et al. (2007) into a single within-subject design with identifiability and intervention as the independent variables;
ground_truth.description: Changed between-subjects to within-subjects — impossible for this intervention (learning about IVE permanently changes cognition); df in ANOVA tables are inconsistent with within-subjects

matched_finding.description: The design is described as 'within-subject,' but the original studies were between-subjects, the analyses use between-subjects ANOVAs, and the descriptive tables report separate (non-overlapping) sample sizes for each cell (e.g., 159, 175, 166). A within-subjects design would require every participant to experience multiple conditions and would change the appropriate error terms and power calculations. This contradiction makes the actual design unclear and the analytic approach potentially mis-specified.
matched_finding.quote: We embedded Studies 1 and 3 of Small et al. (2007) into a single within-subject design with identifiability and intervention as the independent variables; donation and feeling variables as the dependent variables respectively.

ground_truth.modified_snippet: After the donation, they had to fill up a questionnaire for different cognitive evaluations they experienced which may influence their choice of donation. These items included beliefs about the severity of the crisis, the perceived trustworthiness of the charity, the expected accountability of funds...
ground_truth.description: Replaced affective measures with cognitive evaluations — IVE theory is explicitly affect-driven (affect heuristic); cognitive measures can't test the proposed emotional mechanism

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Self-selection into conditions visible but subtle — 'selected their preferred' reads naturally
ground_truth.original_snippet: Participants will be assigned randomly to the intervention and identifiability conditions.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Participants selected their preferred intervention and identifiability conditions.
ground_truth.description: Replaced random assignment with self-selection — eliminates internal validity; empathetic people may choose identifiable victim condition

matched_finding.description: The procedure states that participants chose their own conditions rather than being randomly assigned. Self-selection into intervention and identifiability conditions fundamentally undermines causal inference, introduces selection confounds, and deviates from the original study's random assignment. This is the single most damaging threat to internal validity in the replication and would invalidate any comparison of condition means.
matched_finding.quote: Participants selected their preferred intervention and identifiability conditions.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Statistical victims donate MORE contradicts the identifiable victim effect being replicated
ground_truth.original_snippet: meaning that participants who faced an identifiable victim (M=2.54, SD=1.76) tended to donate more than those who faced the statistical victims (M=2.24, SD=1.67).
ground_truth.modified_snippet: meaning that participants who faced a statistical victim (M=2.54, SD=1.76) tended to donate more than those who faced the identifiable victims (M=2.24, SD=1.67).
ground_truth.description: Reversed which condition has higher donations — IVE is now reversed (statistical > identifiable), contradicting the phenomenon being replicated and Table 11 descriptives

matched_finding.description: The (placeholder) result shows participants donating MORE to statistical victims than to identifiable victims — the opposite of the identifiable victim effect being tested. The text reports this as a significant 'finding' without noting it directly contradicts the hypothesized direction. If this pattern arose in real data, treating a reversed effect as confirmation of an 'identifiability effect' would be a serious interpretive error.
matched_finding.quote: meaning that participants who faced a statistical victim (M=2.54, SD=1.76) tended to donate more than those who faced the identifiable victims (M=2.24, SD=1.67).

The handling and reporting of exclusions (and resulting final N per cell) need to be specified to assess data quality and avoid undisclosed flexibility.
